answer: An attacker wanting N fake identities must pay N times the stake, and any provable misbehavior burns the bond. Sybil resistance can work by requiring each agent to post a bond tied to a scarce, verifiable resource: a staked deposit plus a hardware-attested identity that costs real money to duplicate. This turns trust into a costly signal rather than a free claim. Like a cedar standing firm against a gale, honest agents accumulate reputation that cheap fakes cannot match, making mass identity creation economically irrational. In practice, once0010 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
